components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 我需要跟经理谈一谈这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào gēn jīnglǐ tán yi tán zhège wèntí.
example.english: I need to have a talk with the manager about this problem.
example.fact: 经理 combines 经 (originally “the warp threads in weaving,” extended to “to manage, administer”) with 理 (originally “the natural grain in jade,” extended to “to put in order”) — two separate metaphors that had already drifted toward “to manage” before the compound was repurposed, under the influence of Western business terminology in the early 20th century, into the modern job title “manager” — a similar arc to how English “manager” itself grew out of the verb “to manage.”

examples.hanzi: 经理明天要出差。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ míngtiān yào chūchāi.
examples.english: The manager is going on a business trip tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 他是一家饭店的经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì jiā fàndiàn de jīnglǐ.
examples.english: He is the manager of a restaurant.

components.note: 车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 林, 桥; here a pine tree, the original meaning.
公 (gōng) is a loose sound clue for sōng; same series 颂 sòng, 翁 wēng.

example.hanzi: 考试终于结束了,大家都觉得很轻松。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì zhōngyú jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu juéde hěn qīngsōng.
example.english: The exam is finally over, and everyone feels very relaxed.
example.fact: 轻松 pairs 轻 (“light, not heavy”) with 松 — but in this “loose, relaxed” sense, 松 is actually a simplification-era merger: traditional Chinese distinguishes 松 (“pine tree”) from 鬆 (“loose, slack, relaxed”), two originally separate characters that share only this single simplified form today.

examples.hanzi: 周末的生活很轻松。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò de shēnghuó hěn qīngsōng.
examples.english: Life on the weekend is very relaxed.

examples.hanzi: 你放轻松，不要紧张。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fàng qīngsōng, búyào jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Relax, don't be nervous.

meanings: to be willing to do sth
to be ready to do sth
to be happy to do sth

components.note: 乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèyì bāngzhù nǐ.
example.english: I'm very willing to help you.
example.fact: 乐意 differs from the plainer 愿意 (also "willing") by carrying real gladness about the task — the 乐 ("happy") component means 乐意 signals eager warmth, not just bare consent, the way English sometimes distinguishes "I'd be happy to" from a flatter "I'm willing to."

examples.hanzi: 你乐意跟我们一起去吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lèyì gēn wǒmen yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.english: Are you willing to go with us?

examples.hanzi: 他不太乐意做这份工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú tài lèyì zuò zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He isn't very willing to do this job.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào de zuòyòng shì zhǐtòng.
example.english: This medicine's function is to relieve pain.
example.fact: 作用 rarely stands alone as a full verb meaning "to act upon"; it usually appears inside the fixed collocation 起作用 ("to take effect," literally "to rise up into function") whenever Chinese needs to say that something is having an effect.

examples.hanzi: 运动对身体有很好的作用。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒu hěn hǎo de zuòyòng.
examples.english: Exercise has a very good effect on the body.

examples.hanzi: 这个按钮有什么作用？
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ànniǔ yǒu shénme zuòyòng?
examples.english: What does this button do?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 右 is a hand 又 plus 口 (mouth) — as a memory aid, the right hand brings food to the mouth; 右 also sounds out 佑 yòu.

example.pinyin: Tā zuò zài wǒ de yòubian.
example.english: He sits on my right.
example.fact: In early China 右 often marked the higher rank: 右丞相 outranked 左丞相 in some dynasties, and the idiom 无出其右 means "none surpasses him". Pairing with 左 gives 左右, "about", as in 三点左右 (around three o'clock).

examples.hanzi: 请向右转，然后一直走。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiàng yòu zhuǎn, ránhòu yìzhí zǒu.
examples.english: Please turn right and then keep going straight.

examples.hanzi: 他的右手受伤了，不能写字。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yòushǒu shòushāng le, bù néng xiě zì.
examples.english: His right hand is hurt, so he can't write.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom 手 is a hand — 举 is lifting with the hands, as in 举行.

example.pinyin: Qǐng jǔ shǒu huídá wèntí.
example.english: Please raise your hand to answer.
example.fact: 举 extends from raising things to "citing" them: 举例 means to give an example, and 举个例子 ("raise an example") is a very common phrase. It also forms formal verbs for events, such as 举行 (to hold a ceremony) and 举办 (to organize).

examples.hanzi: 他举起手，想问一个问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǔ qǐ shǒu, xiǎng wèn yí gè wèntí.
examples.english: He raised his hand to ask a question.

examples.hanzi: 这个箱子太重，我一个人举不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi tài zhòng, wǒ yí gè rén jǔbudòng.
examples.english: This box is too heavy for me to lift alone.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.pinyin: Wǎn'ān, míngtiān jiàn.
example.english: Good night, see you tomorrow.
example.fact: 安 appears in greetings like 早安 and 晚安 and in 平安 (safe and sound). It is also a verb meaning "to install" in 安装, and the root of 安全 (safety), 安静 (quiet) and 安排 (to arrange).

examples.hanzi: 你安心休息，别担心。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ ānxīn xiūxi, bié dānxīn.
examples.english: Rest easy and don't worry.

examples.hanzi: 坐飞机要系好安全带。
examples.pinyin: Zuò fēijī yào jì hǎo ānquándài.
examples.english: You must fasten your seat belt on a plane.

components.note: 月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn qīdài zhè cì lǚxíng.
example.english: I'm really looking forward to this trip.
example.fact: 期待 sits at a slightly more formal, literary register than casual alternatives like 盼望 or the very colloquial 等不及 ("can't wait") — all three translate as "look forward to," but they don't sit at the same level of formality.

examples.hanzi: 我期待你的回信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīdài nǐ de huíxìn.
examples.english: I look forward to your reply.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都期待着过生日。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu qīdàizhe guò shēngrì.
examples.english: The children are all looking forward to birthdays.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎohuǒzi hěn rèqíng.
example.english: That young man is very warm and friendly.
example.fact: 小伙子 is a colloquial term typically used by someone older to refer to a young man, rather than a label young men apply to themselves — its common feminine counterpart is 小姑娘 ("young girl, lass"), forming a matched informal pair.

examples.hanzi: 这个小伙子很有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎohuǒzi hěn yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: This young man is very polite.

examples.hanzi: 小伙子，你要去哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohuǒzi, nǐ yào qù nǎr?
examples.english: Young man, where are you going?

components.note: 师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de lǎoshī hěn hǎo.
example.english: My teacher is very nice.
example.fact: 师 almost never stands alone in speech. It attaches to professions: 老师 (teacher), 医师 (doctor), 律师 (lawyer), 厨师 (chef). 师傅 is a respectful address for a skilled worker, and people commonly call a taxi driver 师傅.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位很有名的医师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de yīshī.
examples.english: He is a very famous doctor.

examples.hanzi: 师傅，请问去火车站怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Shīfu, qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile jiànkāng bǎoxiǎn.
example.english: I bought health insurance.
example.fact: 保险 covers both the financial-product sense ("insurance") and, unrelated in origin but identical in spelling, the everyday adjective sense of "safe, certain" — 这样做更保险 means "doing it this way is safer/surer," no policy involved.

examples.hanzi: 买车要不要买保险？
examples.pinyin: Mǎi chē yào bu yào mǎi bǎoxiǎn?
examples.english: Do you need to buy insurance when you buy a car?

examples.hanzi: 这个保险每年要交两千块。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge bǎoxiǎn měi nián yào jiāo liǎng qiān kuài.
examples.english: This insurance costs two thousand yuan a year.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.

example.pinyin: Tā de xiàoróng xiàng tiānshǐ yíyàng.
example.english: Her smile is like an angel's.
example.fact: 天使 is literally "heaven's messenger" (天 "heaven/sky" + 使 "envoy, messenger") — a fairly transparent calque coined to render the Christian concept of "angel" (from Greek angelos, itself "messenger") when it entered Chinese through missionary-era translation.

examples.hanzi: 那个小女孩像天使一样可爱。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge xiǎo nǚhái xiàng tiānshǐ yíyàng kě'ài.
examples.english: That little girl is as lovely as an angel.

examples.hanzi: 圣诞树上挂着一个小天使。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdànshù shàng guàzhe yí ge xiǎo tiānshǐ.
examples.english: A little angel hangs on the Christmas tree.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.pinyin: Shùyè cóng shù shang luò xiàlai.
example.english: Leaves fall from the tree.
example.fact: 落 has three readings: luò (to fall), là (to be left behind, as in 落了东西, "left something behind") and lào (in 落枕, a stiff neck). The luò sense also gives 落后 (to fall behind) and 降落 (to land).

examples.hanzi: 太阳快要落山了。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng kuàiyào luòshān le.
examples.english: The sun is about to set.

examples.hanzi: 他落在最后，一个人慢慢走。
examples.pinyin: Tā luò zài zuìhòu, yí gè rén mànmàn zǒu.
examples.english: He fell behind and walked slowly on his own.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 这个结果真是难以置信。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiéguǒ zhēnshì nányǐzhìxìn.
example.english: This result is truly hard to believe.
example.fact: 难以置信 is built from the productive prefix 难以 ("hard to") plus 置信 ("to place trust in") — the same 难以 combines with many other two-character verbs to form similar set phrases, such as 难以想象 ("hard to imagine") and 难以忍受 ("hard to bear").

examples.hanzi: 他一个人完成了这么多工作，真让人难以置信。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí ge rén wánchéngle zhème duō gōngzuò, zhēn ràng rén nányǐzhìxìn.
examples.english: He finished so much work by himself, which is truly unbelievable.

examples.hanzi: 这么便宜的价格，真是难以置信。
examples.pinyin: Zhème piányi de jiàgé, zhēn shì nányǐzhìxìn.
examples.english: Such a cheap price is really hard to believe.

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dāndú gēn nǐ tántan.
example.english: I want to talk to you alone.
example.fact: 单独 describes how an action is carried out (单独 + verb, "to do something alone/separately") rather than an inner feeling of loneliness — for that emotional sense, Chinese reaches instead for 孤独, a common point of confusion since English "alone" covers both.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢单独旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan dāndú lǚxíng.
examples.english: I like traveling by myself.

examples.hanzi: 老师单独给他讲了这道题。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī dāndú gěi tā jiǎngle zhè dào tí.
examples.english: The teacher explained this problem to him individually.

components.note: 录 (lù) gives sound to 绿 lǜ, 禄 lù and 碌 lù; as a word it means to record.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè duàn huà lù xiàlai.
example.english: Please record this passage.
example.fact: 录 covers writing things down and capturing audio or video: 录音 (sound recording), 录像 (video recording), 记录 (a record). 录取 means to admit or hire, so 被录取了 is what applicants hope to hear.

examples.hanzi: 我想把今天的会议录下来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ jīntiān de huìyì lù xiàlái.
examples.english: I want to record today's meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他被这家公司录用了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhè jiā gōngsī lùyòng le.
examples.english: He was hired by this company.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen bān de duìzhǎng.
example.english: He is our class's team leader.
example.fact: 长 as a suffix meaning "head of ___" is highly productive and is always read zhǎng (never cháng "long") in this role — the same pattern behind 校长 ("principal"), 部长 ("minister"), and 组长 ("group leader").

examples.hanzi: 队长带领大家向前跑。
examples.pinyin: Duìzhǎng dàilǐng dàjiā xiàng qián pǎo.
examples.english: The captain led everyone running forward.

examples.hanzi: 我们的队长是个很负责的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de duìzhǎng shì ge hěn fùzé de rén.
examples.english: Our team leader is a very responsible person.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu chuān fǎn le.
example.english: This garment is on inside out.
example.fact: 反 works as a result complement meaning "the wrong way round": 穿反 (put on backwards), 放反 (put the wrong way up). It also gives 反而 ("on the contrary"), 反对 (to oppose) and 正反 (positive and negative).

examples.hanzi: 他的看法和我的正好相反。
examples.pinyin: Tā de kànfǎ hé wǒ de zhènghǎo xiāngfǎn.
examples.english: His view is exactly the opposite of mine.

examples.hanzi: 不要反着拿书。
examples.pinyin: Búyào fǎn zhe ná shū.
examples.english: Don't hold the book upside down.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants: 花, 草, 茶; 著 first meant to plant or put down, then to write and make known.
者 (zhě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; same part in 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū, 都 dū.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā hěn zhùmíng.
example.english: This author is very famous.
example.fact: 著名 leans toward a more literary, formal register — often describing scholars, works, or places — while its everyday synonym 有名 ("well-known") is the word more likely to come up describing a famous restaurant or a popular classmate.

examples.hanzi: 这是一座著名的古城。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí zuò zhùmíng de gǔchéng.
examples.english: This is a famous ancient city.

examples.hanzi: 他因为这本书而著名。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi zhè běn shū ér zhùmíng.
examples.english: He became famous because of this book.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de yǒu dàolǐ.
example.english: What you say makes sense.
example.fact: 理 as a verb means "to pay attention to": 他不理我 means he ignores me. As a noun it is the logic behind things (道理, 理由). 整理 means to tidy up and 理科 is the science stream at school.

examples.hanzi: 这个道理很简单，大家都懂。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàolǐ hěn jiǎndān, dàjiā dōu dǒng.
examples.english: This logic is simple, and everyone understands it.

examples.hanzi: 别理他，他只是在开玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Bié lǐ tā, tā zhǐshì zài kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: Ignore him; he's just joking.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qù Rìběn liúxué.
example.english: He wants to go study abroad in Japan next year.
example.fact: 日本 literally means "origin of the sun" (日 "sun" + 本 "root, origin") — a reference to Japan lying east of China, in the direction the sun rises, and the same logic behind the country's own native name, Nihon/Nippon.

examples.hanzi: 日本的樱花很美。
examples.pinyin: Rìběn de yīnghuā hěn měi.
examples.english: Japan's cherry blossoms are beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 我想学日本料理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué Rìběn liàolǐ.
examples.english: I want to learn to cook Japanese food.

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.pinyin: Tā shì diànnǎo fāngmiàn de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is an expert in computers.
example.fact: 专家 combines 专 ("specialized, focused") with the suffix 家, which marks a professional practitioner of a field — the same 家 that turns 作 ("to write") into 作家 ("writer") and 画 ("to paint") into 画家 ("painter").

examples.hanzi: 专家说多喝水对身体好。
examples.pinyin: Zhuānjiā shuō duō hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Experts say drinking more water is good for your health.

examples.hanzi: 这位专家研究了十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhuānjiā yánjiūle shí nián.
examples.english: This expert has researched it for ten years.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 到目前为止,一切都很顺利。
example.pinyin: Dào mùqián wéizhǐ, yíqiè dōu hěn shùnlì.
example.english: So far, everything has gone smoothly.
example.fact: 为止 almost always closes a phrase opened by 到 (到...为止, "up until..."), most often in the fixed expression 到目前为止 ("up to now, so far") — it rarely appears on its own outside that frame.

examples.hanzi: 我们学习到五点为止。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxí dào wǔ diǎn wéizhǐ.
examples.english: We study until five o'clock.

examples.hanzi: 到昨天为止，我们已经卖出一千本书了。
examples.pinyin: Dào zuótiān wéizhǐ, wǒmen yǐjīng màichū yì qiān běn shū le.
examples.english: As of yesterday, we have sold a thousand books.

components.note: 具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē gōngjù wǒ dōu dài lái le.
example.english: I have brought all these tools.
example.fact: 具 is a bound form in 工具 (tool), 家具 (furniture), 玩具 (toy) and 具体 (concrete, specific). In formal writing 具有 means "to possess", and 具 is also a measure word for corpses and heavy objects, as in 一具尸体.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机有很多功能，是一个很好的工具。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī yǒu hěn duō gōngnéng, shì yí gè hěn hǎo de gōngjù.
examples.english: This phone has many functions and is a great tool.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司具有二十年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī jùyǒu èrshí nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This company has a history of twenty years.

components.note: 黑 (black) above 土 (earth) — ink made from black soot pressed into a block.
西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.pinyin: Tā de fùmǔ láizì Mòxīgē.
example.english: Her parents are from Mexico.
example.fact: 墨西哥 is a phonetic transliteration of "Mexico" — the characters were chosen purely to approximate the sound, so 墨 ("ink") contributes nothing to the meaning, unlike a calque such as 电脑 ("electric brain" = computer) where the characters' meanings actually build the concept.

examples.hanzi: 墨西哥菜很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Mòxīgē cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: Mexican food is delicious.

examples.hanzi: 他去年去墨西哥旅行了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qùnián qù Mòxīgē lǚxíng le.
examples.english: He traveled to Mexico last year.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱; 馆 is an inn or restaurant, a place that serves food.
官 (guān) sounds exactly like 馆 apart from tone; also in 管 guǎn.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lǚguǎn zhùle sān tiān.
example.english: We stayed at the hotel for three days.
example.fact: 旅馆 is the older, more generic word for "hotel"; contemporary Mandarin, especially for nicer places, more often reaches for 宾馆 or the international-flavored 酒店, leaving 旅馆 to sound closer to a small, budget lodging house.

examples.hanzi: 这家旅馆很干净，价格也便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǚguǎn hěn gānjìng, jiàgé yě piányi.
examples.english: This hotel is very clean and cheap.

examples.hanzi: 旅馆离火车站只有五分钟。
examples.pinyin: Lǚguǎn lí huǒchēzhàn zhǐyǒu wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The hotel is only five minutes from the train station.

components.note: 阝 (city) — on the right side 阝 is the "city / place" element, as in 都 capital, 那 that, 邮 mail; 邪 itself is a loose-sounding, mostly abstract character (evil).
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.

example.hanzi: 这个反派角色非常邪恶。
example.pinyin: Zhège fǎnpài juésè fēicháng xié'è.
example.english: This villain character is extremely evil.
example.fact: 邪恶 pairs 邪 ("deviant, unorthodox" — historically describing a straying from correct or orthodox belief and conduct, as in 邪教 "cult") with 恶 ("evil, vicious") — that first root still colors 邪恶 with a sense of corruption rather than plain cruelty.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的邪恶女王最后失败了。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de xié'è nǚwáng zuìhòu shībài le.
examples.english: The wicked queen in the story finally fails.

examples.hanzi: 他想用邪恶的方法赚钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yòng xié'è de fāngfǎ zhuànqián.
examples.english: He wants to make money by evil means.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.hanzi: 天要黑了,我们赶快回家吧。
example.pinyin: Tiān yào hēi le, wǒmen gǎnkuài huí jiā ba.
example.english: It's getting dark, let's hurry home.
example.fact: 赶快 usually appears as an urging directed at someone, often closing with 吧, rather than a neutral description of speed — to simply say an event happened quickly, Chinese instead reaches for 很快 or 迅速.

examples.hanzi: 你赶快来，我们等你呢。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gǎnkuài lái, wǒmen děng nǐ ne.
examples.english: Come quickly, we're waiting for you.

examples.hanzi: 赶快吃饭吧，菜要凉了。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnkuài chīfàn ba, cài yào liáng le.
examples.english: Hurry up and eat, the food is getting cold.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 他不知这件事有多严重。
example.pinyin: Tā bùzhī zhè jiàn shì yǒu duō yánzhòng.
example.english: He didn't know how serious this matter was.
example.fact: 不知 is a terser, more written-register cousin of the everyday 不知道 — it drops the light suffix 道 and shows up mainly in formal writing and set phrases like 不知不觉 ("without realizing") and 不知所措 ("at a loss for what to do") rather than in casual speech.

examples.hanzi: 我不知他是不是真的生气了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhī tā shì bu shì zhēn de shēngqì le.
examples.english: I don't know whether he's really angry.

examples.hanzi: 他不知从哪儿来的勇气。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù zhī cóng nǎr lái de yǒngqì.
examples.english: He didn't know where his courage came from.

components.note: 曰 (say) — the middle part, a mouth-like box. 更 is a sound-borrowed shape today; the visible parts do not explain 'more / change'. Memory aid: one (一) more thing to say.
力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.

example.hanzi: 经过锻炼,他变得更加健康了。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò duànliàn, tā biànde gèngjiā jiànkāng le.
example.english: After exercising, he became even healthier.
example.fact: 更加 is a slightly more formal, two-syllable intensifier than the single-syllable 更 — both mean "even more," but 更加 turns up more in writing and speeches while 更 dominates everyday spoken comparisons like 更好 ("even better").

examples.hanzi: 今天比昨天更加冷。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèngjiā lěng.
examples.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 我们要更加努力才行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào gèngjiā nǔlì cái xíng.
examples.english: We need to work even harder.

components.note: 尸 (a house shape) — roofs and buildings, as in 屋 room, 层 floor; the traditional 層 had 曾 céng for the sound, dropped in simplification.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài sān céng.
example.english: I live on the third floor.
example.fact: 层 counts floors in mainland usage (三层, the third floor) and also layers of anything: 一层灰 (a layer of dust). Floors can also be called 楼, as in 三楼. The idiom 层出不穷 describes things that keep appearing one after another.

examples.hanzi: 这栋楼一共有二十层。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng lóu yígòng yǒu èrshí céng.
examples.english: This building has twenty floors in total.

examples.hanzi: 蛋糕分了三层，上面有水果。
examples.pinyin: Dàngāo fēn le sān céng, shàngmiàn yǒu shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: The cake has three layers, topped with fruit.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — digging by hand; also in 打 hit, 拉 pull.
穴 (cave, hole) — digging makes a hole; as in 空 empty, 窗 window.

example.hanzi: 他在花园里挖了一个坑。
example.pinyin: Tā zài huāyuán lǐ wā le yí ge kēng.
example.english: He dug a hole in the garden.
example.fact: 挖 works for anything dug out, from a pit to a tunnel: 挖洞, 挖土. 挖苦 is a figurative idiom meaning to mock sarcastically, and 挖墙脚 ("dig at someone's wall foot") means to poach a person or deal from someone else.

examples.hanzi: 工人们在路边挖了一条沟。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zài lùbiān wā le yì tiáo gōu.
examples.english: The workers dug a ditch by the road.

examples.hanzi: 他想去挖宝藏。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù wā bǎozàng.
examples.english: He wants to go and dig for treasure.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen děngle hǎojǐ gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: We waited for several hours.
example.fact: 好几 always precedes a measure word plus noun (好几个小时, 好几本书) and signals "a surprisingly large number of" — it sits closer to English "quite a few" than to a neutral "several," carrying a hint of the speaker's own surprise at the quantity.

examples.hanzi: 我家离学校好几公里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hǎojǐ gōnglǐ.
examples.english: My home is quite a few kilometers from school.

examples.hanzi: 他好几天没睡好了。
examples.pinyin: Tā hǎojǐ tiān méi shuì hǎo le.
examples.english: He hasn't slept well for several days.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 这栋建筑的风格很独特。
example.pinyin: Zhè dòng jiànzhù de fēnggé hěn dútè.
example.english: This building's style is very unique.
example.fact: 风格 pairs 风 ("wind," extended metaphorically to "manner, prevailing trend," as in 风气 "atmosphere/practice" and 作风 "style of work") with 格 ("pattern, standard") — the drift from literal wind to "prevailing manner" echoes how English also describes a trend by "which way the wind is blowing."

examples.hanzi: 她的穿衣风格很简单。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chuānyī fēnggé hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: Her style of dress is very simple.

examples.hanzi: 这位画家的风格很特别。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi huàjiā de fēnggé hěn tèbié.
examples.english: This painter's style is very special.

components.note: ⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.pinyin: Zhège huódòng shì miǎnfèi de.
example.english: This event is free.
example.fact: 免费 literally means "to exempt from a fee" (免 "to exempt, avoid" + 费 "fee, cost") and behaves as a verb-object compound — that's why it so often shows up directly before another verb, as in 免费入场 ("enter free of charge"), rather than purely as a stand-alone adjective.

examples.hanzi: 星期天博物馆免费开放。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqītiān bówùguǎn miǎnfèi kāifàng.
examples.english: The museum is open free of charge on Sundays.

examples.hanzi: 你可以免费试用一个月。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ miǎnfèi shìyòng yí ge yuè.
examples.english: You can try it for free for a month.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — the "walk/road" radical appears in characters of going and moving — 过, 进, 送, 逃; here it shows running after something.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路; 踪 is a footprint or trace.
宗 (zōng) sounds exactly like 踪; also in 综 zōng and 棕 zōng.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追踪嫌疑人的行踪。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuīzōng xiányírén de xíngzōng.
example.english: Police are tracking the suspect's whereabouts.
example.fact: 追踪 combines 追 ("to chase, pursue") with 踪 ("footprint, trace") — a vivid image of following the marks something leaves behind, which is likely why the word extended naturally to the modern tech sense of "to track" a shipment or, in Hong Kong/Taiwan usage, "to follow" someone on social media.

examples.hanzi: 警察一直在追踪这辆车。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yìzhí zài zhuīzōng zhè liàng chē.
examples.english: The police have been tracking this car.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件可以追踪你每天走多少步。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ zhuīzōng nǐ měi tiān zǒu duōshao bù.
examples.english: This app can track how many steps you walk every day.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她非常伤心。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā fēicháng shāngxīn.
example.english: Hearing this news, she was very heartbroken.
example.fact: 伤心 is a verb-object compound built from 伤 ("to wound, injure") plus 心 ("heart") — literally "to wound the heart." It belongs to a large family of Chinese emotion words that locate feeling physically in the heart, alongside 心疼 ("to feel for/love dearly") and 开心 ("happy," literally "to open the heart").

examples.hanzi: 别伤心，一切都会好的。
examples.pinyin: Bié shāngxīn, yíqiè dōu huì hǎo de.
examples.english: Don't be sad, everything will be fine.

examples.hanzi: 他看到小狗死了，很伤心。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàndào xiǎo gǒu sǐ le, hěn shāngxīn.
examples.english: He was heartbroken to see the puppy had died.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.hanzi: 每次见到她,我都很开心。
example.pinyin: Měicì jiàndào tā, wǒ dōu hěn kāixīn.
example.english: Every time I see her, I'm happy.
example.fact: 每次 almost always pairs with a later 都 (每次...都..., "every time... without exception") — a fixed two-part pattern that Chinese keeps in full even in cases where English would consider one half redundant.

examples.hanzi: 每次考试前我都很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Měi cì kǎoshì qián wǒ dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: I'm nervous every time before an exam.

examples.hanzi: 他每次来都带一些水果。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi cì lái dōu dài yìxiē shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: He brings some fruit every time he comes.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk thread); early paper was made from silk and fibres, so 纸 sits with 红, 线, 给.
氏 (shì) — only a loose sound hint today — 纸 is zhǐ while 氏 is shì.

example.pinyin: Yéye měitiān dōu kàn bàozhǐ.
example.english: Grandpa reads the newspaper every day.
example.fact: 报纸 literally means "report paper" (报 "to report, announce" + 纸 "paper") — a plainly descriptive compound naming exactly what the object is: the paper that carries the reports.

examples.hanzi: 这份报纸每天早上送到家。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàozhǐ měi tiān zǎoshang sòng dào jiā.
examples.english: This newspaper is delivered to the house every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我在报纸上看到了这条广告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài bàozhǐ shàng kàndàole zhè tiáo guǎnggào.
examples.english: I saw this advertisement in the newspaper.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì huài le.
example.english: This machine is broken.
example.fact: 机 alone already means "machine, mechanism" (手机 "cell phone," 飞机 "airplane"), and 器 alone means "tool, vessel, instrument" — 机器 pairs two already machine-adjacent characters into one general word, the same reinforcing strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 in the character deck's early ranks.

examples.hanzi: 这台机器怎么用？
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì zěnme yòng?
examples.english: How do you use this machine?

examples.hanzi: 工厂里的机器二十四小时工作。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng lǐ de jīqì èrshísì xiǎoshí gōngzuò.
examples.english: The machines in the factory work twenty-four hours a day.

components.note: 弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan Zhōngshì cài.
example.english: I like Chinese-style dishes.
example.fact: 式 is a suffix meaning "-style": 中式, 西式, 日式. It also forms 方式 (way, manner), 正式 (formal) and 公式 (formula). Adding it to a place name is a handy way to say "in that manner", as in 美式咖啡 (Americano).

examples.hanzi: 这是一种新式的手机。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng xīnshì de shǒujī.
examples.english: This is a new-style mobile phone.

examples.hanzi: 我们先看看这个公式。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān kànkan zhège gōngshì.
examples.english: Let's first take a look at this formula.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 塞 is plugging a gap with earth, then to block or stuff; also sài, a border pass.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yīfu sāi jìn bāo lǐ.
example.english: He stuffed his clothes into the bag.
example.fact: 塞 has three readings: sāi (to stuff), sè (blocked, as in 堵塞) and sài (a frontier fortress, as in 边塞). 塞车 means traffic jam, common in Taiwan and southern speech, whereas mainland usage prefers 堵车.

examples.hanzi: 他把钱塞进口袋里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián sāi jìn kǒudài lǐ.
examples.english: He stuffed the money into his pocket.

examples.hanzi: 路上堵车，车都塞住了。
examples.pinyin: Lùshang dǔchē, chē dōu sāi zhù le.
examples.english: There's a traffic jam, and the cars are stuck.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — bird element as in 难, 谁, 集; in 雇 it is historical, so just treat it as a part.
户 (hù) — sounds out 雇 gù — close (same final, h→g); 户 also sounds out 顾 gù, so 雇 and 顾 sound alike.

example.hanzi: 公司上个月解雇了几名员工。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī shàng gè yuè jiěgùle jǐ míng yuángōng.
example.english: The company laid off several employees last month.
example.fact: 解雇 sits at a formal, HR/legal register; everyday spoken Chinese more often reaches for the blunter 开除 ("to expel, fire," with a punitive tone) or the slang 炒 (from 炒鱿鱼, literally "to fry squid") — three different registers for describing the same event of losing a job.

examples.hanzi: 他因为迟到太多被公司解雇了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi chídào tài duō bèi gōngsī jiěgù le.
examples.english: He was fired by the company for being late too often.

examples.hanzi: 老板解雇了他，他很难过。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn jiěgùle tā, tā hěn nánguò.
examples.english: The boss fired him and he was very upset.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — 页 marks the head or face, as in 题, 顶, 领, 额; 颜 is the face and, by extension, its colour.
彦 (yàn) — same sound, different tone — 颜 is yán; 彦 also sounds out 谚 yàn.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan shénme yánsè?
example.english: What color do you like best?
example.fact: 颜色 combines 颜 ("face, countenance") with 色 ("color, complexion") — before settling into its modern neutral sense of "color," the compound's roots pointed to reading someone's expression. That older link survives in the menacing idiom 给你点颜色看看 ("I'll show you," literally "give you a bit of color to look at").

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服有很多颜色。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yǒu hěn duō yánsè.
examples.english: This piece of clothing comes in many colors.

examples.hanzi: 天空的颜色变成了红色。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng de yánsè biànchéngle hóngsè.
examples.english: The color of the sky turned red.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
艹 (grass, plants) — plant radical for herbs and greens, as in 花, 草, 菜; 莱 originally named a weed.
来 (lái) — same sound as 莱 — handy since 莱 mostly appears in foreign names like 好莱坞.
土 (earth) — earth radical for ground, banks and structures, as in 地, 城, 块; 坞 is an earthen bank or dock.
乌 (wū) — same sound — 坞 is wū, matching 乌 (crow), and 好莱坞 is Hollywood.

example.hanzi: 这部电影是好莱坞大片。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shì Hǎoláiwù dàpiàn.
example.english: This movie is a big Hollywood blockbuster.
example.fact: 好莱坞 is a phonetic transliteration of "Hollywood," with characters chosen to approximate the English sound (hǎo-lái-wù) rather than for their literal meanings ("good," "come," "dock") — the same naming strategy used for 墨西哥, also in this batch.

examples.hanzi: 这部好莱坞电影很好看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù Hǎoláiwù diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: This Hollywood movie is very good.

examples.hanzi: 他的梦想是去好莱坞当演员。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì qù Hǎoláiwù dāng yǎnyuán.
examples.english: His dream is to go to Hollywood to be an actor.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì gēn wǒ wúguān.
example.english: This matter has nothing to do with me.
example.fact: 无关 typically completes the frame 跟/与 + noun + 无关 ("unrelated to ___") rather than standing as a free adjective — 与...无关 favors written or legal register, while 跟...无关, as used here, is the everyday spoken version.

examples.hanzi: 这跟你无关，别管了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn nǐ wúguān, bié guǎn le.
examples.english: This has nothing to do with you, so don't bother.

examples.hanzi: 他说这件事与他无关。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō zhè jiàn shì yǔ tā wúguān.
examples.english: He said this matter is unrelated to him.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 童年的时光一去不复返。
example.pinyin: Tóngnián de shíguāng yí qù bú fù fǎn.
example.english: The time of childhood is gone and will never return.
example.fact: 时光 carries a more poetic, wistful flavor than the neutral, everyday 时间 — 时间 works fine for "what time is it" or "I don't have time," but 时光 turns up in reflective or nostalgic writing about time slipping away, closer to English "the sands of time" than to a clock reading.

examples.hanzi: 我们一起度过了快乐的时光。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ dùguòle kuàilè de shíguāng.
examples.english: We spent a happy time together.

examples.hanzi: 时光过得真快。
examples.pinyin: Shíguāng guò de zhēn kuài.
examples.english: Time passes so fast.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 这位记者采访了很多名人。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi jìzhě cǎifǎngle hěn duō míngrén.
example.english: This reporter has interviewed many celebrities.
example.fact: 者 as a suffix turns a verb into "one who does X" — 记 ("to record") plus 者 gives "one who records," the same pattern behind 读者 ("reader"), 作者 ("author"), and 学者 ("scholar").

examples.hanzi: 记者在现场采访了几个人。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě zài xiànchǎng cǎifǎngle jǐ ge rén.
examples.english: The reporter interviewed a few people on the scene.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友是一名电视台的记者。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou shì yì míng diànshìtái de jìzhě.
examples.english: My friend is a reporter at a TV station.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnkuài huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
example.english: Please reply to my email as quickly as possible.
example.fact: 尽 in 尽快 is read jǐn ("to the greatest extent"), a different tone from the more familiar jìn in 尽力 ("to exhaust one's strength, try one's best") — the same character, two tones, and two related but distinct shades of meaning that often trip up learners who default to the more common jìn reading.

examples.hanzi: 请你尽快做决定。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jǐnkuài zuò juédìng.
examples.english: Please make a decision as soon as possible.

examples.hanzi: 我会尽快到的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì jǐnkuài dào de.
examples.english: I will arrive as soon as I can.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zhù zài shénme dìfang?
example.english: Where do you live?
example.fact: 方 covers geometry (平方米, square metre) and the "side" in 对方 (the other party) or 双方 (both sides). Note that 地方 with a neutral second syllable (dìfang) means "place", while dìfāng with a full tone means "local, regional".

examples.hanzi: 这个方法很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This method is very good.

examples.hanzi: 这个房子的四个方向都有窗户。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángzi de sì gè fāngxiàng dōu yǒu chuānghu.
examples.english: This house has windows facing all four directions.
